newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow trading on Thursday, dealers said.
They said volume was thin in lacklustre late trading.
"I think people have squared positions for year-end," one U.S. bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,362.25/62.40 at close against an opening of 2,362.0/63.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,361.25/62.00 and 2,361.50/62.00, respectively.
Dealers said operators were reluctant to take up any fresh positions because they could have trouble squaring positions in the thin year-end market.
They said there was no reaction seen in the market on reports over riots in the west Java town of Tasikmalaya.
Indonesian rioters set ablaze at least three Christian churches, several other buildings and cars in the small town on Thursday afternoon, a police official and residents said.
The reason for the attacks was not immediately clear.
"There are not so many people around to react on the news. They have gone on holidays or stayed squared," one dealer said.
Swap premiums remained soft on the back of sustained ample rupiah supply in the afternoon money market.
Overnight money fell to six percent from seven percent.
Bank Indonesia offered overnight papers at six percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.10/0.15 and tom/next at 0.65/0.75.
One-month swaps was at 13.25/14.00, two at 26.50/28.50, three at 39.5/41.0 and six at 84.00/85.50 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,358/2,550 and the conversion rate to 2,358/2,406 on Thursday.
